angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 606,442 km at 155.62 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.4260 +/- 0.0124 mas (same row, RUWE 0.84): 155.62 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.8717 +/- 0.0064 solar radii from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-538 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract): 606,442 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.892 +/- 0.051 solar masses from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-538 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5534 +/- 61 K from Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-538 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-538 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...677A..33B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-538.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.508, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
